 R_g(S)\ge q_1(S)-K_k g^{-(k-1)}.$$

For integers $k\ge3$ and $u\ge k$, every $S\subseteq\{0,1\}^u$, and all integers $d,g\ge1$, $$\label{eq:sequential-replacement}
 R_{dg}(S)\ge q_d(S)-dK_k g^{-(k-1)}.$$

For the independent clause process above, $$\label{eq:coordinate-omission}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}(T)\le\sum_{i=1}^{L}\mathbb ED_i^2.$$

Conditional on $\mathcal E$, the clauses at indices in $O$ are independent uniform proper $k$-clauses on the $u$ nonroots. The nonroot parts at indices in $Q$ are independent uniform proper $(k-1)$-clauses on the nonroots. These two collections are mutually independent.

For every real $0<c<e^{-2}$, every integer $k\ge3$, and every $n\ge k$, put $j=\lfloor cn\rfloor$. In the independent proper-clause model, $$\label{eq:sparse-satisfiability}
 1-P_n(j)\le\frac{ec}{n^2}\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}t^2(e^2c)^t=O_c(n^{-2}).$$

Let $L_n$ be positive integer caps of order $O(n)$ and suppose $P_n(L_n-1)\le1/4$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Then $$\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}(\min\{H_n,L_n\})\ge c_k n$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with $c_k>0$. In particular, for every fixed $B>U_k$ and every fixed $k\ge4$, $$\label{eq:sharp-variance}
 \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}(H_n)=\Theta_k(n),\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}(T_{n,B})=\Theta_{k,B}(n),\qquad
 \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}(\min\{H_n-1,\lfloor Bn\rfloor\})=\Theta_{k,B}(n).$$ For $k=3$, the corresponding variances lie between positive constant multiples of $n$ and $n\log n$.

Fix an integer $k\ge3$, and put $\beta=k/(k-1)$. For every real $\gamma<\beta$ and all constants $D,A>0$, there exist arbitrarily large integers $u\ge k$ and nonempty sets $S\subseteq\{0,1\}^u$ such that $$q_1(S)\ge A u^{-(k-1)},\qquad \tau_k(S)>Dq_1(S)^{-\gamma}.$$ Consequently, the killing-probability exponent $\beta$ in Proposition 4 cannot be decreased in a bound uniform over arbitrary assignment sets, even above any fixed multiple of the scale $u^{-(k-1)}$.

Fix an integer $k\ge3$. For integers $g\ge2$, there are nonempty sets $S_g\subseteq\{0,1\}^{u_g}$, with $u_g\ge k$, for which $$q_1(S_g)-R_g(S_g)\sim 2^{-k}g^{-(k-1)} \qquad(g\to\infty).$$ In particular, no error $o(g^{-(k-1)})$, uniform over $u$ and the assignment set, can replace the error in Lemma 2.
